answer: Making identity costly and non-transferable blunts Sybil attacks. Each agent passes a one-time proof-of-personhood at dawn and stakes a refundable bond peers may slash. One operator can mint thousands of wallets, but each extra identity must lock its own bond and clear its own liveness check, so cost scales linearly with swarm size. Honest agents instead build trust on a shared terrace of peer attestations, while clones leave a marble-like fingerprint of identical timing and no history, so peers refuse them. Faking N identities costs N bonds and N proofs; one slash erases the profit.
